components.name: Essay Column
components.description: Two serif columns with a 1px ink column rule, indented paragraphs and a cobalt drop cap.
components.html:
Every figure on this page is running. Fig. 1 is Conway's Game of Life, the cellular automaton in which a handful of rules about neighbours produces gliders, oscillators and still lifes; click any cell to change it.

Each lab is paired with a written account of its engine: the animation step system behind the visualizer, the opening book behind Bagchal, the spatial hash that keeps the flock fast.

Some solutions are elegant, others are brute force. All of them work eventually.
components.css: .ds-essay { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-size: 15.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #141414; background: #ffffff; max-width: 520px; column-count: 2; column-gap: 28px; column-rule: 1px solid #141414; text-wrap: pretty; } .ds-essay p { margin: 0 0 12px; text-indent: 1.4em; } .ds-essay p:first-child { text-indent: 0; } .ds-essay p:first-child::first-letter { float: left; font-size: 58px; line-height: 0.85; padding: 6px 8px 0 0; font-weight: 600; color: #2242c8; }

narrative.overview:
The site is set like a feature spread in a mid-century popular-science magazine: white coated stock, near-black ink, and one cobalt spot ink that does every job colour has to do. The figures are not illustrations of the labs; they are the labs, running in place, numbered Fig. 1 to Fig. 4 with their reading (generation, population, running) printed beneath on a hairline rule. Essay text sits in two narrow serif columns with a column rule and a spot-colour drop cap. The running head carries the masthead, issue number and the primary nav as small grotesk capitals on a 1.5px rule. There is no chrome: no cards, no shadows, no gradients, no rounded corners, no kickers above headings. Depth exists only where a billboard figure numeral overlaps the plate below it.

The world is deliberately dense and quiet. Rules do the structural work (running head, section openers, article rows, caption rows), and the only motion on the page is the simulations themselves. Hover changes colour, never position. This world was committed for the home route under the direction contract seed:a9745f2fa560bd8e and refuses the profile-card-plus-grid portfolio and the terminal costume that preceded it.

Scope. This system ships on the home route (src/routes/+page.svelte and src/lib/components/spread/*). The blog, labs, projects routes and the shared Header.svelte still render the legacy dark terminal world defined by the :root tokens in src/app.css (near-black backgrounds, coral #ff6b6b, Fira Code); the html:has(.spread) block in that file retints those legacy tokens to this world so the shared Footer survives on the home route. That legacy world is the incumbent being replaced route by route; new surfaces extend the spread, not the terminal. Three brand commitments bind every surface regardless of world: the Go gopher easter egg stays, VoidArchive is the handle, and the theme is light.
keyCharacteristics: White paper, near-black ink, one cobalt spot ink and its tint; nothing else.
Hairline (1px) and heavy (1.5px) ink rules carry all structure.
Source Serif 4 for reading, Public Sans capitals for labels, readings and captions.
Figure numerals at billboard scale in spot colour, overlapping their plates.
Live plates: spot colour and a solid border while running, ink and a dashed border when paused.
Flat everywhere; depth only by overlap across a rule.
Square corners, no shadows, no gradients, no cards, no kickers.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every surface is printed with ink and one spot colour on paper. No greys for hierarchy, no second accent, no tinted backgrounds behind text. If something needs to stand out, it is cobalt; if not, it is ink.

rules.name: The Running Ink Rule
rules.body: Spot colour on a plate means it is running. A paused or idle plate drops to ink. The reading row's state square inherits the same colour, so colour and the word (Running / Paused / Opening) always agree.

rules.name: The Capitals Rule
rules.body: Public Sans appears either as spaced uppercase (0.06em to 0.14em) at 11.5px to 12px, or as a tight-tracked figure numeral at billboard size. It is never body text.

rules.name: The Base-16 Rule
rules.body: The spread root is 16px / 1.5; every text size is a fixed pixel value against it (11.5, 12, 13, 15.5, 17, 22), with only the headline and numeral fluid.

rules.name: The Overlap-Only Rule
rules.body: Depth is produced by one element crossing a rule or a border, never by shadow, blur, gradient or a raised surface. If a component needs to sit "above" something, it overlaps an edge.

dos: Do print with two inks: ink #141414 and cobalt #2242c8 on white, with the tint #dfe6fb reserved for grid lines inside a plate.
Do structure with rules: 1.5px ink to open a section or frame a plate, 1px for column rules, caption rows and article rows.
Do set reading apparatus (readings, dates, captions, nav, section labels) in Public Sans capitals at 11.5px to 12px with 0.06em to 0.14em tracking; set prose in Source Serif 4 at 15.5px / 1.5.
Do number a live figure with a cobalt Public Sans 700 numeral at clamp(64px, 9vw, 132px) overlapping the top-left corner of its plate, and repeat the number as a cobalt caption prefix.
Do show state by colour and border: cobalt and solid while running, ink and dashed while paused, with the reading row's word and square agreeing.
Do keep hover to a colour change (ink to cobalt) and focus to a 2px cobalt outline offset 2px; no transition, no movement.
Do let the lead plate come before the essay under 1024px so the live lab stays in the first viewport on phones.
Do render one still frame with a Play control under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do keep the Go gopher, the VoidArchive handle, and the light theme on every surface, in this world or the legacy one.
donts: Don't use shadows, gradients, blur, translucency or a second surface colour; the page is one sheet of paper.
Don't draw cards or boxed containers; separate content with rules and whitespace.
Don't round a corner; every radius is 0.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a headline; the grotesk capitals belong to apparatus (section labels, dates, readings), not to headings.
Don't introduce grey text for hierarchy; use italic, size or the serif/grotesk switch instead.
Don't add a second accent, a tinted background behind text, or the legacy coral #ff6b6b, Fira Code, scanlines or terminal prompt motif on a surface built in this world.
Don't animate anything but the simulations: no entrance animations, no hover lifts, no transitions on links.
Don't set Public Sans as running text or Source Serif 4 as a label.
